FINAL BUZZER

Basketball School

## FINAL BUZZER

is our closing huddle where coaches see the players off as a group. The Final Buzzer should take no more than 5 minutes to maximize player's attention spans. There are five parts that should be covered in every Final Buzzer:

CALL IN

Players are verbally called in to huddle up and stand in a circle with all players and coaches if numbers allow (for larger groups, coaches may need to stand in front of the players).

CONNECTIONS

Players are given connections by the coaches as they join the Tip-Off (example of connections: high five, fist bump, handshake, pat on the shoulder).

COMMUNICATIONS

Players are delivered any relevant news or information for the day. This can include rules, expectations, directions to the bathroom, expectations for water break, etc.

CONCLUSION

Players are debriefed on the learnings and prepared for the end of the module.

CHEER

Players and coaches give an enthusiastic and excited cheer together! "NBA Basketball School on 3! (Location Name) on 6!"

MODULE 9: FULL OUTLINE

WARM-UP

Basketball School

STEAL THE CONE

12 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available space (no baskets needed)

### EQUIPMENT

1 cone per group. Can add 1 ball per player for dribbling loads.

### DESCRIPTION

Players will work in groups of three. Use every center circle and paint area in the gym. If there are not enough circles or paint areas in the gym for the number of players, use extra cones to mark out grids of the same size. Place the cone in the middle of their playing area with a defender next to it. The other two players must spread out along the outside of the area in any location. The defender must protect the cone from being touched by the perimeter players. The perimeter players attempt to touch the cone with their hands or feet, but they are only allowed to enter the area for a maximum of three seconds. Change the defender each time the cone is tagged.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Change the movement pattern (e.g. hopping, skipping, etc.).
- Add a second cone, a second defender, and a third attacker.
- Add a ball for dribbling.

### STAFF ROLE

- Ensure the players keep and communicate score.
- Make sure players start from different angles and locations.
- Remind players to transition quickly and take advantage after a score (offense touch half-court, defense touch 3PT line).

### SCORING

N/A

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Learning about deceptive movements

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "How could you trick or distract the defender?"

WARM-UP

Basketball School

STEAL THE TAIL GATE TAG

12 MIN

BINDING YES NO

### PLAYING SPACE

All available space (no baskets needed)

### EQUIPMENT

1 bib per player, 6 cones per group

### DESCRIPTION

Players can work in groups of anywhere from four to eight players. Each group should work in an area equivalent to half of the half-court. Use six cones to create three cone gates in random areas, separated by a small distance of approximately one step. Two offensive players will start outside the area, with bibs tucked into their shorts. Two defenders will start anywhere inside the workspace. As soon as the offense steps inside, they have to step through as many gates as possible until their bibs are pulled out. The goal is to get as many points as possible by passing through gates until both players have their bibs pulled. The offense should keep going until both players are out. After both players exit, a new team of two comes in. The defense stays for four repetitions before changing roles.

### EXAMPLES OF LOADS

- Play the same game while dribbling.
- Play 3-on-3.

### STAFF ROLE

- Create the cone gates. These can be moved around in different locations throughout the course of the game.
- Ensure the offense starts outside of the workspace in different locations.

### GUIDING QUESTIONS

- "What tactics could you invent defensively or offensively to make this easier?"

### SCORING

1 point for each gate passed as a team.

### KEY CONCEPTS

- Developing agility and teamwork

GAME TIME

Basketball School

## GAME TIME

is where players participate in different activities and games designed to stimulate their growth and development.

These activities have been carefully created to mimic the game of basketball. With the NBA Basketball School Camp Curriculum, players develop technically and tactically through the actual act of playing basketball itself.

Each Game Time activity is clearly described and presented in the following format: name, time, space, equipment, description, scoring, types of loads, staff roles, key concepts, and guiding questions. Coaches are encouraged to utilize the information presented and to expand on those ideas in a way that would be most meaningful to their players.

2-ON-2+ GRAB AND PLAY

3-ON-3 AROUND THE CONE

2-ON-1 I MORE

3-ON-3 RANDOM POSSESSION CHANGE

4-ON-4 CHANGING RIMS

2-ON-2+ CLOSEOUTS

5-ON-5 LOADS-BASED
